# M2 production configuration preparation

Prepared on 2026-09-23. No production variables or deployments were changed by this preparation. PR [#22](https://github.com/guy915/Co-Scientist/pull/22) still needs a real passing required CI run before release.

The campaign-owned bearer subject is `campaign-external-reference-2026`. Its new access code, session signing secret, and MCP shared secret are held only in `/Users/guy/Library/Application Support/CoScientist Campaign/m2-release-secrets.json` (directory `0700`, file `0600`), outside the repository. The file contains no production API key or private research data. Never print its values, copy it into a checkout, or include it in a deployment log. `AUTH_MODE` remains at its existing `compatibility` default so other users retain their current access path. Production currently has no `AUTH_SECRET`, `RESEARCHER_ACCESS_CODES`, `CAMPAIGN_RESEARCHER_IDS`, or `COSCIENTIST_MCP_SHARED_SECRET` variable on the API, and no shared-secret variable on MCP.

The API's deployed `MCP_SERVER_URL` is exactly `http://mcp.railway.internal:8888/mcp`; use that value for `COSCIENTIST_CAMPAIGN_MCP_URL`. Both the deployed September 10 API client and MCP server already understand `COSCIENTIST_MCP_SHARED_SECRET`. The prepared identity mapping is one JSON object from the subject to its access code; `CAMPAIGN_RESEARCHER_IDS` is a JSON array containing only that subject. Keep global `COSCIENTIST_REQUIRE_FREE_MODELS` unset to preserve explicit BYOK; campaign bearer requests use persisted request-scoped policy in the intended release.

When required CI passes, stage the API secret, identity, exact campaign URL, and selected free model values with Railway's `variable set --stdin --skip-deploys`, validating rendered values in-process without printing them. Redeploy the API first and check health and authenticated MCP access. Then stage the same MCP secret on the MCP service, redeploy MCP, and check that unauthorized calls fail while the API still reaches it. This order prevents the MCP service from requiring a header the serving API does not yet send. Keep the four model roles on the exact selected zero-priced route and recheck its current catalog eligibility before any inference. Merge the PR only after the paired configuration and CI checks are both verified; then observe both auto-deployed services and run the release smoke checks. If staging or either old-code redeploy fails, restore the previous nonsecret settings and stop before the merge. Never print or restore a paid route as a recovery shortcut.

The restricted credential file remains available for the later release cycle. Its contents must not be committed. The verified pre-migration database backup and code rollback target are recorded in `m2-production-backup.json`.
